post_reveal_reason: At N65 the signed-real H0 phase also survives (chi2=1.32069, p=0.25047), so a repeated (12+5i)/13 angle cannot distinguish H0 from the selected H8 alias.
question: At an independent Gaussian norm and a new angle, which single signed-real transport law, if any, survives among H0, H4, and H8?

observer.normalizer: probability per paired configuration; the same Pinson-Arguin tau=i baseline is subtracted from both embeddings

projective_invariant.uncertainty: delete-one-batch jackknife; diagnostic only, the frozen decision uses the three GLS gates

assumptions: N65 fitted H8 coordinates transported separately to the two N145 physical frames

production.common_field_within_n145_pair: the same counter-derived 290-bit Bernoulli vector is applied to both deterministic primal-edge orders for every replica

score.covariance: full paired 4x4 covariance of the mean from 100 held-out batches
score.fit: GLS profile over one complex base amplitude and one signed-real gain per candidate
score.single_stop_rule: Exactly one model may be selected: unique H8 pass -> H8_OBSERVER_HARMONIC_SELECTED; unique H0 pass -> H0_EVEN_CHARACTER_SELECTED; unique H4 pass -> H4_SELECTED; zero or multiple passes -> STOP_MIXED_OR_UNRESOLVED

boundaries: The N65 H0 test was post-reveal; N145 is the first frozen three-model held-out gate.
The N^-1 prediction is used for design and power only; held-out scoring profiles all amplitudes.
The invariant X is a readable phase fingerprint, not a second evidence vote.
Common random bits are a covariance coupling, not a claimed physical edge isomorphism.
Smoke runs and cost estimates cannot change the production sample count, seed, batch count, score, or stop rule.
